persuasive-sales.name: Persuasive Sales
persuasive-sales.summary: Top-of-funnel sales arc that creates awareness and alignment with a prospective customer. Anchored in a market change, leading to your unique capabilities, supported by proof, ending with a clear call to action.

beats.name: Introduction
beats.description: Open with a brief framing of who you are and why this conversation is worth the prospect's next thirty minutes. Keep credentials short; the audience cares about their problem, not your résumé.

beats.name: Big Change
beats.description: Name the market shift the prospect's industry is living through. Make it concrete, recent, and undeniable. The change — not the product — is the reason they should care.

beats.name: Winners and Losers
beats.description: Show how the change is creating winners and losers in the prospect's space. Use named examples where you can. The goal is for the prospect to wonder which side they'll end up on.

beats.name: Benefits
beats.description: Paint the outcome a winner experiences: a vivid picture of the prospect's life on the other side of the change. Lead with what changes for them, not with what your product does.
beats.instructions: Describe benefits, paint a vivid picture

beats.name: Capabilities
beats.description: Reveal the unique capabilities that make those outcomes possible. Frame them as the 'magic gifts' the prospect needs to win the new game. Highlight what's structurally different from the alternatives.
beats.instructions: Present unique features as 'magic gifts' to the customer

beats.name: Evidence
beats.description: Share customer testimonials, case studies, and measurable outcomes from organizations like the prospect's. Pick evidence that maps to the benefits you promised, not generic logos.

beats.name: Call to Action
beats.description: Ask for the next step in the sales process. Be specific: a pilot, a workshop, a follow-on conversation with a named stakeholder. Make the smallest credible commitment that keeps momentum.

beats.name: Close
beats.description: Close with a final image and contact path. Leave the prospect with one line about why they're better off acting now than later, and clear instructions for how to engage.

all-hands.name: All Hands
all-hands.summary: The full company — mixed roles, mixed seniority, looking for context, signal, and inclusion.
all-hands.description: An all-hands audience spans the whole company. Frame the period in terms anyone can grasp: what we did, what mattered, and what's next. Highlight people and teams; surface successes and challenges; close on a forward-looking note. Avoid lapsing into function-specific jargon.

educate.name: Educate
educate.summary: Teach a concept, process, product, or domain so the audience can use it correctly.
educate.description: Use when the primary job is learning. Structure around concepts, examples, practice, and checks for understanding rather than persuasion or reporting.
educate.outcome: The audience understands the material well enough to apply it.

technical.name: Technical
technical.summary: Precise, evidence-led voice for engineering, research, and product-detail audiences.
technical.description: Lead with the question or claim, then walk through the mechanism and the numbers. Use exact terminology; assume the audience can handle and prefers it. Diagrams, tables, and benchmarks are first-class.
voiceCues: State the claim, then the mechanism, then the evidence.
Use exact terminology — don't soften technical terms for general readability.
Quote benchmarks with conditions (cold/warm, p50/p95/p99, dataset, hardware).
Prefer diagrams and tables over prose paragraphs for structural information.
samplePhrases: p95 inference latency is 38ms on a single A100, down from 312ms on the prior runtime.
We replaced the streaming serializer with a batched protobuf path; throughput rose 4.2× under load.
The result holds for context windows up to 32k tokens; beyond that, see appendix B.

bold.name: Bold
bold.description: A vibrant, high-energy theme with bold colors and a dynamic, attention-grabbing style. Great for presentations that need to stand out.

deep-purple.name: Deep Purple
deep-purple.summary: Purple-led palette for innovation and premium positioning.
deep-purple.description: A focused purple palette for decks that need to feel creative, distinctive, and premium.

burnt-orange.name: Burnt Orange
burnt-orange.summary: Warm orange and red accents for energetic commercial decks.
burnt-orange.description: A warm, high-contrast palette built around burnt orange, red, navy, and gold. It feels active without losing structure.

grandview.name: Grandview
grandview.description: Grandview is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Grandview Display for headings with Grandview for body text.

impact.name: Impact
impact.description: Impact is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Impact for headings with Grandview for body text.

title-subtitle.name: Title Subtitle
title-subtitle.summary: Reach for it when a headline needs one supporting line, as on a cover or a section opener.
title-subtitle.description: A title with a subtitle beneath it. Use it for the cover slide, for section openers, or for a closing slide with a headline and a short follow-up line.

text-3x.name: Text 3x
text-3x.summary: Reach for it when three parallel points each need a short passage of their own.
text-3x.description: A title above three text blocks in a row, equal in weight. Use it for three pillars, three steps explained in prose, or three options described one by one.

chart-3x.name: Chart 3x
chart-3x.summary: Reach for it when three charts tell one story, each with its own note.
chart-3x.description: A title above three charts, each followed by a text block, in three columns. Use it for a small-multiples view of three metrics, regions or cohorts.

list-3x.name: List 3x
list-3x.summary: Reach for it when three groups of points need their own lists.
list-3x.description: A title above three lists in a row. Use it for three themes, three phases or three audiences, each with a few bullets.
